page: Amazon Web Services t4g.xlarge is a burstable virtual machine instance powered by the custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, has a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks reflect its burstable nature and ARM architecture. In single-core stress-ng tests, the processor achieves an average score of 1519.58, while multi-core performance is weaker at 6011.97. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large blocks, with read speeds of 66.09 GB/sec and write speeds of 32.48 GB/sec, though small block cached reads are weaker at 233.41 GB/sec. Cryptographic operations are supported via hardware-accelerated AES, but the instance lacks AVX, AVX512, and AMX instruction sets, resulting in poor scores on complex decompression tasks like bzip3 and lower performance in LLM inference tests.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t4g.xlarge offers a budget-friendly profile for workloads with variable CPU utilization. Because it uses a burstable CPU allocation model, it is highly cost-effective for applications that remain idle or run at low baseline levels but require occasional bursts of full CPU power. This makes it suitable for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 4.66 GB/sec, lightweight database operations, Redis caching, and development or testing environments that do not require sustained high-performance compute resources.
description: Amazon Web Services t4g.xlarge is a burstable, general-purpose instance powered by a 4-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 16.0 GB of RAM, a 1 Gbps baseline network speed, and no local storage or GPU. The instance delivers average single-core CPU performance and large-block memory bandwidth, though multi-core and complex decompression tasks show weaker benchmark results. Lacking AVX and AMX extensions, it is not designed for heavy vector math or machine learning. Instead, its burstable CPU allocation makes it a highly cost-efficient option for workloads with variable demand. It is best suited for static web serving, Redis caching, development environments, and lightweight database operations that benefit from a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio without requiring continuous maximum CPU utilization.
